angle: the machine's own rule as a physical thing: what turning each knob would do to a real object
subject: A real wet pane seen at an angle and cut through at its right edge, so the glass shows its thickness as a hatched section and the heavy bead sitting on the cut shows its meniscus in profile, holding as much water as the puddle lets it.
controls: rate: how many drops strike the face of the pane (count of foreshortened beads, sparse at 0.25 a beat to crowded at 8).
roof: how tall the wet band is on the glass (position/extent along the pane's height): every bead sits at its note's height, so 0 st is one line of beads and 36 st wets most of the pane.
gust: the incoming drops' streaks slant and the runs on the face drift sideways along the pane (shape, the trails bend toward or away from the cut).

puddle: the bead on the cut swells (scale of its profile and meniscus, about 1.5x from 0 to 100) because a fuller glass holds more before it lets go; when it does go, its run sweeps the face and replays what it took in.
reference: opxy/reference patent-section language as used in craft.md (hatching for cut material); library/theseus-tower for black-over-outline bodies
risks: The section is a narrow strip at the right edge: at 1:1 it can read as a post or a pipe rather than the glass's thickness, and the pane's other edges aren't drawn, so the angle is carried only by the foreshortened beads.
The subject (the bead on the cut) sits at the edge, not where the eye lands first; the bead field in the middle competes with it.
Gust's sideways push runs mostly along the camera's depth axis, so it's foreshortened; it needs checking at ±100 that it clears the 24 px floor.
Muted: no drops strike, the profile bead drops from G7 to G4 and the hatched section stays as the only clear structure.
